question: Who builds the supply network: what writes provinces_by_supply_order and in what order, what assigns supply_depot_id, and what computes supply_depot_distance

addresses.name: CSupply::ResetSupplyOrder
addresses.comment: Refills provinces_by_supply_order (+0x54) from the province vector (+0xB8C..+0xB90), one pointer per province in province-id order. The whole body is a single copy loop. Called at 0x282CF8 immediately before the qsort at 0x282D18 that puts the array in farthest-from-depot order, and at 0x27E537 right after +0x54's storage is allocated at 0x27E52A as count*4 bytes.
addresses.evidence: The body is 0x45 bytes and does nothing else: bound from ([eax+0xB90]-[eax+0xB8C])>>2, then `mov edx,[[eax+0xB8C]+ecx*4]; mov esi,[eax+0x54]; mov [esi+ecx*4],edx`. Both call sites load the game state into eax first (`mov eax,ebx` at 0x282CF6 and 0x27E535); ecx is the loop counter, not a this. Bare ret, no stack arguments. Shown wrong by a call site that puts something other than CCurrentGameState* in eax, or by +0x54 not being the supply order array.

addresses.name: CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork
addresses.comment: Recomputes every province's supply_depot_distance. Clears the dirty flag at CCurrentGameState +0x50, then sweeps the province vector: supply_depot_hops (+0x50) is zeroed, and supply_depot_distance (+0x4C) is set to 100000 where the province already carries a depot label and its template's +0x13D is set, and to 0 otherwise. A second sweep calls CSupply::SpreadFromDepot (0x289BE0) for every province whose supply_depot_id equals its own id - that is what makes a province a depot. It never writes supply_depot_id; that is CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot (0xA70C0). Reached from CInGameIdler::Enter at 0x25C611, after the loop there has given every unlabelled province a depot, and from 0x282630 at 0x2826E8 and 0x282CEF, each guarded on CCurrentGameState +0x50.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly of 0x289B20..0x289BDE: `mov byte [esi+0x50], dl` with edx zero; per province `mov [eax+0x50],edx`, `cmp [eax+0x48],edx / je`, `cmp byte [[eax+0xD4]+0x13D],dl / je`, then `mov [eax+0x4C],edi` with edi=0x186A0 or `mov [eax+0x4C],edx`; then `cmp [eax+0x48],edi / jne` against the loop index and `call 0x689BE0`. esi holds the state at all three call sites. Bare ret, ecx unused. Shown wrong by a fourth call site that passes the state in some other register, or by +0x50 on the game state turning out not to be the rebuild trigger.

addresses.name: CSupply::SpreadFromDepot
addresses.signature: void __stdcall CSupply::SpreadFromDepot(CCurrentGameState* state, int depot, int depotIndex@EDX)
addresses.comment: The distance relaxation, one depot at a time. Sets the depot's own supply_depot_distance to 0, then works a FIFO queue of 0x10-byte nodes over the template's ProvinceEdge vector (+0x90..+0x94, stride 0x14, neighbour id at edge+4). A neighbour is considered only if its template's +0x13D is set and its supply_depot_id already equals `depot` - the label partitions the map and this only fills in distances inside one partition. The step cost is infrastructure-weighted, not a hop: infra = provinceModifier[MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE] * (1000 + [MODIFIER_LOCAL_INFRASTRUCTURE] + [MODIFIER_GLOBAL_INFRASTRUCTURE]) / 1000, clamped below by a lazily computed constant at rva 0x17EA400 (from the float 10.5 at rva 0x120A680) and above by 1000; then step = max(4000 - 4*infra, 1000) / 1000, an integer 1..4, multiplied by the neighbour's CProvinceTemplate +0x24. The neighbour is relaxed only when its current distance is strictly greater, and it then also gets supply_depot_hops = parent's hops + 1.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly of 0x289BE0..0x289E27. `ret 8` with [ebp+8]=state and [ebp+0xC]=depot; the caller at 0x289BBE pushes edi then esi and also does `mov edx,edi`, so edx repeats the depot id and is used once, at `mov esi,[[eax+0xB8C]+edx*4]`. The modifier indices are [province+0x114]+0x60/0x68/0x70 with stride 8, so 12/13/14, which ghidra/modifierIds.json gives as MODIFIER_INFRASTRUCTURE, MODIFIER_LOCAL_INFRASTRUCTURE, MODIFIER_GLOBAL_INFRASTRUCTURE. 0xB99980 is used elsewhere in the same function as a divide by 1000 of a 64-bit product, and 0xB99AF0 is the multiply feeding it. Shown wrong if +0x114 is not the province modifier's value array, or if 0xB99AF0/0xB99980 are not _allmul/_alldiv - either would change the cost formula but not the shape of the relaxation.

addresses.name: CompareProvincesByDepotDistanceDescending
addresses.comment: The qsort comparator for provinces_by_supply_order. Returns +1 when b's supply_depot_distance is the larger, 0 when equal, -1 otherwise - a descending sort on +0x4C, so element 0 is the province farthest from its depot. This is the derivation of the 'farthest first' in CCurrentGameState::provinces_by_supply_order's name, which CSupply::DailySupplyPass's single forward sweep depends on.
addresses.evidence: The whole function is 0x2A bytes: eax = (*[ebp+0xC])->+0x4C, ecx = (*[ebp+8])->+0x4C, `cmp eax,ecx; jle` returning 1, else `setge dl; lea eax,[edx-1]` returning 0 or -1. It is the fourth argument to the CRT qsort at 0x282D18, whose element size is 4 and whose base is state+0x54. Shown wrong only by 0xB96750 not being qsort - and that call cleans 0x10 bytes for four arguments and the array is read back sorted immediately after.

addresses.name: SupplyOrder_CallQsort
addresses.comment: qsort(state->provinces_by_supply_order, provinceCount, 4, CompareProvincesByDepotDistanceDescending) - the one place the supply order array is sorted. The instructions after it read back element 0's supply_depot_distance into CCurrentGameState +0x58, clamp it to 500, and where it exceeded 500 re-run CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot on that farthest province.
addresses.evidence: 0x282D0C..0x282D18 pushes 0x67B100, 4, (provinces_end-provinces_begin)>>2 and [ebx+0x54], calls 0xB96750 and cleans 0x10. Shown wrong by 0xB96750 not being qsort.

addresses.name: CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot
addresses.comment: Assigns this province's supply_depot_id - the supply network's label - and marks the network dirty. Does nothing unless the owner's country id (+0x330) is non-zero and the area at +0x2B4 answers true to its virtual slot 0 (CNullOwnerArea does not). The area gets first refusal: where area+0x70 is non-null and either (area+0x70)+8 is above 1 or area+0x69 is 1, a non-zero (area+0x70)+0x10 becomes the label. Otherwise the label comes from CCountry::FindSupplyDepot (0xF2B00) called on the controller's country. Afterwards out_of_supply_days (+0x20) is incremented when the label came out 0 and zeroed when it did not, and g_CCurrentGameState +0x50 is set to 1 so the next tick rebuilds the distances. Called per province from CInGameIdler::Enter at 0x25C557 for every province still carrying label 0, from 0x282D3B on the farthest province when its distance exceeded 500, and from 0x9EF5B, 0xA3546 and 0xB8279.
addresses.evidence: Disassembly of 0xA70C0..0xA7202: it is the only writer of [province+0x48] found by a linear sweep of the whole .text for stores to [reg+0x48] and [reg+0x4C], and both of its stores land there. Bare ret, ecx is this, no stack arguments. The name is a reading of what it does rather than a recovered symbol. Shown wrong by another writer of supply_depot_id existing - the sweep decodes .text linearly and restarts after bad bytes, so a store inside a region it mis-aligned on could have been missed - or by +0x20 not being out_of_supply_days.

addresses.name: CCountry::FindSupplyDepot
addresses.signature: int __thiscall CCountry::FindSupplyDepot(CCountry* this, CProvince* province, void* visited, CCountry* origin)
addresses.comment: Answers the province id that a province should draw supply from, or 0. Returns the origin country's acting_capital_province_id (CCountry +0xE24) once the province's area matches that of the origin's own acting capital, and otherwise recurses into the countries reached through the area's list at +0x34 and through +0xF34/+0xF38 on the country, carrying the same origin and a visited list so the walk terminates. `origin` defaults to `this` when it is passed null. This is what makes two provinces share a supply_depot_id: they resolve to the same acting capital.
addresses.evidence: `ret 0xC` for the three stack arguments; ecx is this; the caller at 0xA713C loads it from the controller tag through CCountryTag::GetCountry (0x2610). Both return paths that are not `xor eax,eax` load [ebp+0x10]+0xE24, which project.json already names acting_capital_province_id, guarded by comparing [province+0x2B4] against [0x42F100(country)+0x2B4]. The recursion is the two `call 0x4F2B00` sites at 0xF2C41 and 0xF2CF8. The name is a reading; what the +0x34 list and +0xF34/+0xF38 actually are (allies, lend-lease, puppets) was not established, so which other countries' capitals can end up labelling a province is not settled.

struct_fields.name: supply_network_dirty
struct_fields.comment: set to 1 whenever CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot changes a province's supply depot label, and cleared by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork; the two rebuild sites in 0x282630 are both `cmp byte [state+0x50], 0; je` around the call
struct_fields.evidence: written 1 at 0xA71D9 and 0xA71F3 (the two arms of the 'is there a game state yet' branch at the end of CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot) and 0 at 0x289B34; read only at 0x2826DA and 0x282CE7, each immediately before `call 0x289B20`. Shown wrong by another writer, or by 0x289B20 not being the rebuild.

struct_fields.name: max_supply_depot_distance
struct_fields.comment: the largest supply_depot_distance on the map, taken from element 0 of provinces_by_supply_order right after the sort and clamped to 500. It is not the end pointer of the +0x54 vector - +0x54's storage is a plain new[] at 0x27E52A and its length is recomputed from the province vector everywhere it is walked. Where the raw value exceeded 500 the game also re-runs CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot on that farthest province, which is how a province cut off at 100000 gets a fresh depot label.
struct_fields.evidence: 0x282D1D..0x282D3B: `mov ecx,[ebx+0x54]; mov eax,[ecx]; mov eax,[eax+0x4C]; mov [ebx+0x58],eax; cmp eax,0x1F4; jle; mov [ebx+0x58],0x1F4; mov ecx,[ecx]; call 0x4A70C0`. No reader of +0x58 was found through g_CCurrentGameState, so what consumes it is not settled. Shown wrong by a reader that treats it as a pointer.

struct_fields.name: provinces_by_supply_order
struct_fields.comment: every province sorted by supply depot distance, farthest first. Storage is one new[] of provinceCount*4 bytes at 0x27E52A; CSupply::ResetSupplyOrder (0x289AD0) refills it in province-id order and the qsort at 0x282D18 reorders it with CompareProvincesByDepotDistanceDescending. The length is never stored here - every walker recomputes it from provinces_end - provinces_begin.
struct_fields.revises: the farthest-first claim was carried by this comment but never derived; the comparator at 0x27B100 now derives it, and the allocation and sort sites are worth recording beside it
struct_fields.evidence: the comparator returns +1 when the second argument's +0x4C is the larger, which is a descending sort, so CSupply::DailySupplyPass's forward sweep does start at the province farthest from its depot. Shown wrong by 0xB96750 not being qsort, or by a second sort of +0x54 elsewhere.

struct_fields.name: supply_depot_distance
struct_fields.comment: not a hop count - the infrastructure-weighted cost of the cheapest path to the depot, 0 at the depot itself and 100000 while cut off. Each step adds max(4000 - 4*infrastructure, 1000)/1000 - an integer 1..4, worst where infrastructure is lowest - times the entered province's CProvinceTemplate +0x24. Written only by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork (0x289B20, the reset) and CSupply::SpreadFromDepot (0x289BE0, the relaxation). The plain hop count is +0x50. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures
struct_fields.revises: 'steps to the depot' said hop count; the relaxation at 0x289D88 multiplies a per-province cost by an infrastructure-derived factor before adding it, so the units are not hops
struct_fields.evidence: 0x289D77..0x289D8E computes eax = (max(4000-4*infra,1000)/1000) * template->+0x24 + parentDistance and stores it at [neighbour+0x4C] only after `cmp [neighbour+0x4C],eax; jle skip`. Shown wrong if CProvinceTemplate +0x24 were always 1 and the factor always 1, which would make the two readings coincide - +0x24's value was not sampled from a running game.

struct_fields.name: supply_depot_distance
struct_fields.comment: not a hop count - the infrastructure-weighted cost of the cheapest path to the depot, 0 at the depot itself and 100000 while cut off. Each step adds max(4000 - 4*infrastructure, 1000)/1000 - an integer 1..4, worst where infrastructure is lowest - times the entered province's CProvinceTemplate +0x24. Written only by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork (0x289B20, the reset) and CSupply::SpreadFromDepot (0x289BE0, the relaxation). The plain hop count is +0x50.
struct_fields.revises: same correction as CProvince +0x4C: 'steps to the depot' is wrong, the step is weighted
struct_fields.evidence: see CProvince +0x4C; the two structures carry the same offsets.

struct_fields.name: supply_depot_id
struct_fields.comment: province id of the depot it draws from, and the supply network's label: CSupply::SpreadFromDepot only relaxes a neighbour that already carries the same value, and CSupply::DailySupplyPass only moves goods between provinces that do. Written only by CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot (0xA70C0), from the province's area or, failing that, from CCountry::FindSupplyDepot on the controller - which answers the supplying country's acting capital. A province whose supply_depot_id equals its own id is a depot, and is where the distance relaxation starts. CMapProvince derives from CProvince and adds nothing at this offset, so the field is the base's; CProvince's own code reads it. Both carry it because Ghidra has no inheritance between the two structures
struct_fields.revises: adds the one writer and the meaning of depot_id == own id, neither of which was recorded
struct_fields.evidence: a linear sweep of .text for stores to [reg+0x48] found the two in 0xA70C0 and no other on a province; 0x289BB9's `cmp [eax+0x48],edi` against the loop index is the depot test. Shown wrong by a store the linear sweep mis-aligned past.

struct_fields.name: supply_depot_id
struct_fields.comment: province id of the depot it draws from, and the supply network's label: CSupply::SpreadFromDepot only relaxes a neighbour that already carries the same value, and CSupply::DailySupplyPass only moves goods between provinces that do. Written only by CProvince::UpdateSupplyDepot (0xA70C0). A province whose supply_depot_id equals its own id is a depot, and is where the distance relaxation starts.
struct_fields.revises: adds the one writer and the meaning of depot_id == own id

struct_fields.name: supply_depot_hops
struct_fields.comment: the plain hop count to the depot, as against the weighted cost at +0x4C. Zeroed for every province by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork and set to the parent's value plus one each time CSupply::SpreadFromDepot relaxes a neighbour. CSupply::DailySupplyPass never reads it; the only other reader found is 0xDB3CC.
struct_fields.evidence: `mov [eax+0x50],edx` with edx zero at 0x289B5A, and `mov [esi+0x50],edx` at 0x289DA7 where edx is [ebp-0x1C]+1 and [ebp-0x1C] was loaded from the popped province's +0x50 at 0x289C62. A holder-chained scan on the province vector (+0xB8C) for +0x50 returns exactly those two sites plus 0xDB3CC. Shown wrong by a writer reached through some other holder.

struct_fields.name: supply_depot_hops
struct_fields.comment: the plain hop count to the depot, as against the weighted cost at +0x4C. Zeroed by CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork and set to the parent's value plus one by each relaxation in CSupply::SpreadFromDepot.

struct_fields.name: unknown_24
struct_fields.comment: a per-province traversal cost. CSupply::SpreadFromDepot multiplies it by an infrastructure-derived factor of 1..4 to get the step it adds to supply_depot_distance, and 0xB615E does the same thing without the factor - edi = neighbour->template->+0x24 + accumulated, compared against CProvince +0x10 - so it is a distance charged for entering a province, not an edge length (ProvinceEdge already carries its own distance at +0xC). Its actual value was not sampled from a running game, so whether it is normally 1 is open.
struct_fields.evidence: a holder-chained scan on CProvince +0xD4 for +0x24 returns six sites; 0x289CDC and 0xB615E use it as an additive distance, 0xF52E9 and 0x391DA2 are unexamined, and 0x1C91AD is a virtual call through slot 9 while 0x296A09 writes a byte, so those two are false chains. Shown wrong by a loader that puts something else at +0x24, which reading CProvinceTemplate's construction would settle.

struct_fields.name: unknown_flag_13d
struct_fields.comment: tested by the supply pass, the Simplified Terrain loop and the supply network builder; 1 in every province seen; not a land/sea flag. In CSupply::RebuildSupplyNetwork a province with it clear has its supply_depot_distance forced to 0 rather than to the 100000 'not reached yet' value, and in CSupply::SpreadFromDepot such a neighbour is skipped outright - so a province with it clear is never relaxed and never takes part in supply. Still unidentified.
struct_fields.revises: records that the network builder tests it too, and what a clear flag actually does there - the old comment named only two readers
struct_fields.evidence: 0x289B71 `cmp byte [ebx+0x13D],dl` reaching the `mov [eax+0x4C],edx` arm, and 0x289CC8 `cmp byte [eax+0x13D],0; je` skipping the neighbour. Shown wrong by a province with it clear that still gets a distance.

struct_fields.name: unknown_a1c
struct_fields.comment: an embedded CGoodsPool of which only supplies (+0xA24) and fuel (+0xA28) are ever touched - a daily accumulator, added to by CSupply::DailySupplyPass at 0x287671 and 0x287993 with the part of a province's need met by its own current_producing, and by 0x1BBFBA in the unit consumption code; reset along with +0x994..+0x9AC by 0x4F28B0. Deliberately left unnamed: the pass writes production met locally into it and the unit code adds to it as well, and which of the two the field is for was not settled.
struct_fields.evidence: the slot is a CGoodsPool by construction, not by spacing: CCountry's constructor writes the pool vftable at 0xC9302 (`mov [ebx+0xA1C],eax`) and zeroes +0xA24 at 0xC930E, and CGoodsPool puts supplies at +8 and fuel at +0xC, which is exactly 0xA24 and 0xA28. A bare scan of [reg+0xA24] returns 17 sites, six of them real country-pointer uses. Shown wrong by a writer of +0xA2C..+0xA38 (money, oil, metal and the rest) turning up, which would mean it is a general pool rather than a supplies-and-fuel counter.

slots_noted: vtable.py --holding says none of 0xA70C0, 0xF2B00, 0x289AD0, 0x289B20, 0x289BE0 or 0x27B100 is in any class's virtual table; they are all called directly.
